grand_strategy.reading:
Albania runs the strategy of a small state that has bet everything on being
the most useful and best-aligned partner of whoever matters, and on Edi Rama
as the man who makes that bet personal. Every relation in the card follows
from it: NATO and the American channel for security, the EU for the future,
Italy and the UK for the migration currency, the Gulf and the Kushners for
capital, Turkey for arms and religion, Kosovo for the nation. The Luttwak
pattern is that each source of leverage creates a counter-pressure that
lands on the same pillar. The EU path is only as fast as the rule of law
allows, which is the front where Rama fights his own prosecutors; the
Kosovo pact adds to Albania's security and to Serbia's rearmament; the
Trump channel brings the Board of Peace and the Sazan protests together.
In 2026 the EU front is moving (three chapters closed on 14 Jul, the
Commission calling Albania and Montenegro the closest candidates) while the
American front is cooling (the 2027 NATO summit dropped from the draft
text, 10% tariffs). Two signals that are not rows: Albania's own ministers
played down the US embassy's Iran warning of 1 Apr 2026, and Greek
diplomatic sources publicly distanced Athens from Rama's claim at Delphi
that a Hague referral was agreed. The test is whether the EU path survives
the collision between Rama's immunities draft and the benchmarks, with
Greece as a possible veto at the end.

stances.note: Mirrored from Kosovo's own card (XKX stance toward ALB: ally, kin; same sources). No bilateral alliance treaty, but a stable de facto alignment: the 18 Mar 2025 trilateral defence declaration with Croatia, Rama in Pristina on 16 Feb 2026, the free-trade area since 2003. Friction is real - Rama cancelled the 2023 joint government meeting over its format - and unification stays rhetoric: surveys cited by Kosovo Online (2024) put support for a unification referendum at 82.9% in Albania and 70.6% in Kosovo, but neither government has a policy to pursue it. Bond - kin: language and ethnicity; Tirana is Pristina's motherland. Serbia reads this alignment as its 'greatest threat', so the SRB-ALB asymmetry is deliberate.

stances.note: Mirrored from Serbia's side (SRB stance toward ALB: rival, cooling, grievance; same Euronews, A2 and N1 sources). Structural reading: Tirana is Kosovo's motherland and co-signed the 18 Mar 2025 declaration that Vucic called an 'arms race' (Mar 2025) and 'the greatest threat to Serbia' (Munich, Feb 2026); in April 2026 he announced a rearmament programme against the 'Tirana-Zagreb-Pristina alliance'. Cooperation survives at the top - Open Balkan, and a joint Rama-Vucic text in the FAZ on EU accession without veto (Euronews, 11 Mar 2026), which the Commission and member states rejected - so the pair is rival, not adversary: Albania has no aim against Serbia's existence. Rama's rhetoric (a 'reliable partner' to Belgrade) is not the grade. No Albanian source uses the word 'rival': our reading of the structure (confidence C). stances_toward.note: Rival from Moscow's side because Albania sits on the far side of Russia's Serbian file: it recognises Kosovo, which Moscow does not, and has applied the EU sanctions since 2014. Zakharova rebuked Edi Rama in October 2021 for the 'Greater Albania' idea as contrary to UNSC 1244, and Albania is on Russia's 2022 unfriendly list (Government Order 430-r). The contest is in statements, media bans and border turn-backs rather than in interests Moscow must defend by force, and Russia has no lever in Tirana. Not adversary: Moscow has no aim against Albania's existence or regime. Bond none: no kinship claimed in Moscow's telling. Our reading of the structure from Moscow's side (confidence C).

relations_from.summary: Nine member states blocked delivery of the Interim Benchmark Assessment Report on judicial-independence grounds in 2026 before it was adopted; SPAK accused former minister Belinda Balluku of about EUR 251m of losses in road tenders, the governing party refused to lift her immunity, and Rama dismissed her after a Constitutional Court ruling.

sources.title: Rule-of-law concerns - an obstacle to Albania's EU accession
Albania closes its first three negotiating chapters

relations_from.summary: Albania has applied the EU's Russia sanctions since 2014 (decision 597/2025 lists over 2,500 entries), denied entry to 207 Russian nationals between 2022 and April 2026 and blocks RT and Sputnik; as of April 2026 no assets of sanctioned Russians had been identified.

sources.title: Albania's record on sanctions against Moscow

relations_from.summary: Albania cut diplomatic relations with Iran on 7 Sep 2022 after cyberattacks on its government systems that Tirana and the Middle East Institute attribute to Iran's wish to punish the hosting of the MEK. In 2026 the US embassy warned of Iran-linked threats (1 Apr) and Tirana called the warning speculative.

relations_from.summary: Albanian police raided the MEK camp Ashraf-3 near Tirana on 20 Jun 2023 and seized about 150 devices on a judicial order over breaches of the settlement agreement; casualty accounts conflict (the MEK-linked NCRI reported one death, Albanian officials 15 police and 21 MEK injured) and Tehran's claim that the devices went to Iran was denied.
relations_from.note: Casualty figures differ by side; none is adopted.

relations_to.summary: Eagle Hills (Abu Dhabi) signed a EUR 2bn marina and port transformation at Durres in January 2023 (state stake 33%, about 450 hectares); trade press reported 20 months later that the marina project still had no developer.
relations_to.note: An announced figure for a scheme whose financing close and construction start were not found.

relations_to.summary: Mutual visa exemption agreement signed in Tirana in January 2023 for ordinary passports of both countries (stay of up to 90 days according to later visa guidance; early reports gave 3 months).
relations_to.note: Reports differ on the permitted stay (90 days or 180 days); the shorter, later figure is quoted.

sources.title: China, Albania sign mutual visa exemption agreement

relations_to.summary: The Ionian maritime boundary is unresolved: the 2009 delimitation deal was annulled by Albania's Constitutional Court (2010); in October 2020 Dendias and Rama agreed to go to the ICJ, but no text exists and Greek diplomatic sources say delimitation is no longer an immediate priority (May 2026).
relations_to.note: Mirrors the ALB to GRC row (same sources).

relations_to.summary: The 1996 Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation, Good Neighbourliness and Security stays the highest bilateral instrument; Greece's law of war with Albania is formally still in place.
relations_to.note: Mirrors the ALB to GRC row.

relations_to.summary: An Albanian court convicted Fredi Beleri, the Greek-minority mayor-elect of Himara held on remand, of vote-buying (two years, March 2024); Athens called the trial a 'mock trial' and Mitsotakis tied Albania's EU progress to the case (Oct 2023). Rama and Mitsotakis met at the Delphi forum in April 2026 and Rama spoke of a new strategic partnership document within the year.

relations_to.summary: Protocol (Nov 2023) for Italian-run migrant centres at Shengjin and Gjader, converted in March 2025 into repatriation centres (about 620 detainees by mid-June 2026). Advocate General Emiliou (23 Apr 2026) found it compatible with EU law with safeguards; Advocate General Medina (June 2026) stressed that EU guarantees apply to detention outside the EU; the CJEU has not ruled. MEPs said on 29 Jun 2026 they were blocked from fully inspecting Gjader. Mirrors the Albanian card.

relations_to.summary: Law students from three Albanian-language universities began protests in Skopje on 6 Apr 2026 demanding the bar exam in Albanian as well as Macedonian; students and politicians from Albania and Kosovo took part on 18 May, three students were arrested, and DUI's Trajanov called the involvement of citizens from Albania and Kosovo an impermissible external influence. Mickoski called the protest an opposition attempt to destabilise the government.

relations_to.summary: In late August 2026 PM Spajic said the planned closing of EU chapters would coincide with coordinated hybrid activity by at least two regional states; Montenegrin media read it as Albania and Serbia, Albania's foreign minister denied any part ('a friendly NATO ally') and Montenegro told Rama that Albania was not meant. Vucic said he was sure Croatia was one of them.
relations_to.note: Spajic has not named the two countries; the identification of Albania, Serbia or Croatia is press interpretation.

relations_to.summary: The Hague summit (2025) agreed that Albania would host the next meeting after Ankara; a draft of the Ankara declaration dropped the line (30 Jun 2026 reporting), Albania's spending was below 2% in 2025, and Rutte said after Ankara that the next summit will 'certainly' be in Albania but the date is not set; Bloomberg-sourced reports say allies considered skipping 2027. Mirrored from the Albania card.
